CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a patient presenting for evaluation of a kidney stone. One week ago, patient developed sudden onset severe right-sided back pain while working in a barn moving hay. The pain was associated with diaphoresis and nausea, prompting evaluation by his PCP, who ordered a CT scan and found a kidney stone. The pain radiated almost down to the groin. Since the initial episode, pain has occurred intermittently a couple of times but did not last as long. Patient denies current ongoing pain, with tenderness localized to the right side. Patient has been straining urine as instructed and denies seeing anything in the urine. Denies blood in urine or darker urine than usual.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports nausea and diaphoresis associated with initial pain. Denies blood in urine and denies darker urine.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Father has a history of kidney stones.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works with horses; was moving hay in barn when pain developed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs stable, no fever. Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Abdominal examination: no tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. Costovertebral angle tenderness on the right side.

RESULTS
CT scan shows a 0.5 cm stone located in the proximal right ureter with no evidence of hydronephrosis. BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture ordered.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right ureteral kidney stone, 0.5 cm, proximal location. Plan includes: increase fluid intake to facilitate urination and stone passage; oxycodone 5 mg every 6 to 8 hours for pain management; acetaminophen for breakthrough pain; continue urine strainer until stone passes; obtain BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture; prescribe antibiotics if infection identified on urinalysis. Follow-up in 1 to 2 weeks. If stone has not passed by then, discuss lithotripsy as treatment option.
